prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S182: Before entering a conveyor or sorter hazard zone, the Maintenance Technician isolates the relevant energy sources and verifies that movement has stopped.
S183: Guards and access panels remain in place during operation, and bypasses are permitted only under an approved maintenance procedure.
S184: The Baggage Operations Supervisor uses the occupancy note to confirm that a chute can safely accept bags.
S185: The Maintenance Technician consults the Recovery Route Card before returning equipment to service after a route change.
S186: Pebble secures the response area and directs handling of any bag referred for explosives assessment.
S187: The Security Duty Manager coordinates access control when a security response affects equipment or staff movement.
S188: A scanner fault requires the affected feed to be held until the fault is assessed and the bag disposition is known.
S189: The Maintenance Technician checks for jammed bags, damaged belts, sensor obstruction, and signs of mechanical wear before clearing a fault.
S190: Lantern supplies current flight data so that operating routes can be checked against active assignments.
S191: The Baggage Control System records equipment alarms and presents the affected route for review by authorized personnel.
S192: When the Induction Tray Conveyor stops unexpectedly, staff prevent further bag entry and keep the approach area clear.
S193: The Maintenance Technician removes a jam only after confirming isolation and arranging safe access to the blockage.
S194: The Bag Reconciliation Station supports verification when a bag's location or identity is uncertain after an interruption.
S195: East Make-Up Conveyor runs only after its guards are confirmed closed and its downstream capacity is available.
S196: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit is held from receiving bags when its discharge area is obstructed or its operating status is uncertain.
S197: The Maintenance Technician performs corrective work and reports any condition that prevents safe restart.
S198: The Baggage Operations Supervisor controls the operational hold, communicates its scope, and confirms that affected staff understand the restriction.
S199: A recovery begins with a controlled inspection of the affected equipment and confirmation that bags in the area have been accounted for.
S200: If a route or flight assignment has changed, the operator obtains approval before the bag is released into the revised process.
S201: The final disposition and supporting checks are recorded so that later review can trace why the bag returned to the planned process.
S202: Restart requires confirmation that personnel are clear, guards are restored, alarms are understood, and the intended route is available.
S203: Each bag remains under controlled custody from screening release until an authorized loading handoff is confirmed.
S204: The Baggage Control System maintains the bag identity, assigned flight, screening disposition, and current handling status as the authoritative record.
S205: Staff keep bags in monitored areas and prevent access by personnel who are not assigned to the active handling task.
S206: The Induction Tray Conveyor carries only bags with readable identity data and a valid route assignment into the screening process.
S207: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter directs cleared bags to their assigned make-up destination and diverts unresolved items from normal handling.
S208: The North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner must report healthy status before their screening results are relied upon for release.
S209: The Image Resolution Desk reviews images that require operator assessment and records a disposition before the bag can continue.
S210: Any unresolved screening result places the bag in a controlled hold area until the required review is complete.
S211: The Explosives Response Team assesses security events referred for specialist action and communicates the resulting disposition through approved operational channels.
S212: The Secondary Inspection Chute is kept clear of unrelated bags so that identity and custody remain unambiguous during inspection.
S213: The Security Duty Manager uses the seal log to verify that recorded custody seals remain accounted for and that any discrepancy has been escalated.
S214: A Maintenance Technician reports equipment faults that could affect bag identity, screening integrity, or controlled access before the equipment is returned to service.
S215: The Baggage Operations Supervisor confirms that outstanding holds and route exceptions have an assigned owner before authorizing continuation of processing.
S216: Orchard shall release a bag to the next handling stage only when the recorded screening disposition and assigned destination are valid.
S217: The Flight Data Gateway provides the flight and destination data used to check that the bag remains assigned to an operating departure.
S218: The Bag Reconciliation Station compares scanned bag identities against the expected flight population and flags missing or duplicate records for resolution.
S219: The Airline Ramp Coordinator uses the Bag Match Query to review unresolved bag-to-flight mismatches before loading authorization is granted.
S220: The East Make-Up Conveyor moves reconciled bags toward the correct flight position without bypassing required identity checks.
S221: The West Make-Up Conveyor remains subject to the same controlled access and reconciliation rules as other make-up equipment.
S222: The Transfer Bag Feeder accepts transfer bags only when their identity and intended onward flight can be verified.
